To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the National Assessment of Education Progress (NAEP) is a valid measure of educational achievement in the United States, that it has been used to assess the achievement of students in the United States over the last 40 years, and that it is an important measure of the achievement of students from the United States in international comparisons.

(1) NAEP long-term trend scores in reading and mathematics are not a reliable indicator of student achievement in these subjects, and (2) NAEP long-tern trend scores are a reliable indicator of the extent to which student performance in these subjects is being measured in a stable way over time.

the NAEP long-term trend assessments are: • Valid, reliable, and useful measures of student achievement in mathematics, reading, and science; • The only source of national trend data on student achievement; • Not subject to the same political pressures as state tests; and • The only way to assess the effects of the No Child Left Behind Act (NCLB) and other education policies on student achievement over a long period of time.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new generation of assessment instruments for use with students in grades 3, 5, and 7.
the long-term trends of the NAEP scores in the 4th and 8th grade math tests.
the development and evaluation of a computer-based assessment system for use in large-scale testing programs.
